original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-auto-ass-implies-P}
An auto-associated ring $R$ has the following property: (P)
Every proper finitely generated ideal $I \subset R$ has a nonzero
annihilator.
statement:
An auto-associated ring $R$ has the following property: (P)
Every proper finitely generated ideal $I \subset R$ has a nonzero
annihilator.
conclusions:
An auto-associated ring $R$ has the following property: (P)
Every proper finitely generated ideal $I \subset R$ has a nonzero
annihilator.
semantic_review_note: An auto-associated ring has property (P): every proper finitely generated ideal has a NONZERO annihilator. This does not merely assert existence of the zero annihilator.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-P-universally-injective}
Let $R$ be a ring having property (P) of
Lemma \ref{lemma-auto-ass-implies-P}.
Let $u : N \to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
Then $u$ is universally injective if and only if $u$ is injective.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring such that every proper finitely generated ideal of $R$ has a nonzero annihilator.
Let $u : N \to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
Then $u$ is universally injective if and only if $u$ is injective.
hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring such that every proper finitely generated ideal of $R$ has a nonzero annihilator.
Let $u:N\to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
conclusions: $u$ is universally injective if and only if $u$ is injective.
semantic_review_note: Over a ring where every proper finitely generated ideal has a nonzero annihilator, injectivity of a map of projective modules is equivalent to universal injectivity. Both directions and projectivity remain.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-P-fPD-zero}
Let $R$ be a ring. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ has property (P) of
Lemma \ref{lemma-auto-ass-implies-P},
\item any injective map of projective $R$-modules is
universally injective,
\item if $u : N \to M$ is injective and $N$, $M$ are finite projective
$R$-modules then $\Coker(u)$ is a finite projective $R$-module,
\item if $N \subset M$ and $N$, $M$ are finite projective as $R$-modules, then
$N$ is a direct summand of $M$, and
\item any injective map $R \to R^{\oplus n}$ is a split injection.
\end{enumerate}

\item if $u : N \to M$ is injective and $N$, $M$ are finite projective
$R$-modules then $\Coker(u)$ is a finite projective $R$-module,
\item if $N \subset M$ and $N$, $M$ are finite projective as $R$-modules, then
$N$ is a direct summand of $M$, and
\item any injective map $R \to R^{\oplus n}$ is a split injection.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item every proper finitely generated ideal $I\subset R$ has a nonzero annihilator,
\item any injective map of projective $R$-modules is
universally injective,
\item if $u : N \to M$ is injective and $N$, $M$ are finite projective
$R$-modules then $\Coker(u)$ is a finite projective $R$-module,
\item if $N \subset M$ and $N$, $M$ are finite projective as $R$-modules, then
$N$ is a direct summand of $M$, and
\item any injective map $R \to R^{\oplus n}$ is a split injection.
\end{enumerate}
semantic_review_note: Five assertions are equivalent: property (P), injective projective maps are universally injective, finite-projective injections have projective cokernel, finite-projective submodules split, and every injection R→R^n splits. All five are preserved.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coker-injective-free}
Let $R$ be a ring. Suppose that $\varphi : R^n \to R^n$ be an injective
map of finite free modules of the same rank. Then
$\Hom_R(\Coker(\varphi), R) = 0$.
